summary:
2026 Supportive Housing Notice of Funding Availability

OC HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT (OCHCD) announces the release of the 2026 Supportive Housing Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) making available up to $20.9 million dollars of Federal HOME Investment Partnership Program (HOME), HOME American Rescue Plan Program (HOME-ARP), Mental Health Services Act (MHSA)/Behavioral Health Services Act (BHSA), 15G Reserves and Housing Successor Agency (HSA) Funds, to promote the acquisition, new construction, and acquisition/rehabilitation of Supportive Housing and will also provide up to 100 Housing Choice, Mainstream and/or Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing Project Based Vouchers for extremely low-income households who are homeless.

Funds are available until the NOFA closes, is replaced by a new NOFA, or until all available funds are committed via Board of Supervisors action, whichever occurs first. Interested and qualified applicants who can successfully demonstrate their ability to provide supportive housing for extremely low-income households who are experiencing homelessness are encouraged to submit proposals.

Small-scale housing is an eligible activity under this NOFA, so long as it meets NOFA criteria and the guiding principles in the Commission to Address Homelessness Small-Scale Housing Unit Report received and filed by the Board of Supervisors on January 28, 2025.

The NOFA is available at the following County website links:

OpenGov NOFA 2026-01: https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/ocgov/projects/210644

OCHCD Website: https://www.ochcd.org/housing-development/developer/notice-funding-availability

summary:
The primary goal of this program is to provide services to Medi-Cal eligible youth, adults and/or older adults, with a serious mental health condition, often a co-occurring medical/substance use disorders, or stand-alone severe substance use disorder requiring acute inpatient psychiatric treatment in a safe, secured environment to stabilize symptoms occurring as a result of their mental health condition. 

The County intends to establish two (2) Master Contracts which are dependent on State licensure but have the same required services as outlined below, pursuant to which County intends to execute contracts with all applicants who meet eligibility and submission requirements. The Master Contracts will be for one of the following service provisions:

  • Inpatient Behavioral Health Services, for the facilities that are an Acute Free-Standing Psychiatric Hospital (AFSPH)
  • Medi-Cal Mental Health Managed Care Inpatient Hospital Services for the facilities that are a General Acute Care Hospital (GACH)

summary:
The OC Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking applications from licenses hospital emergency departments to develop practical and sustainable protocols to initiate Rapid Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) for people newly diagnosed with HIV or re-engaging in care.

 

Rapid Antiretroviral Therapy (Rapid ART) Protocol Development is intended to support the development of practical, evidence-based protocols that improve linkage to care for individuals newly diagnosed with HIV and people living with HIV (PLWH) who are re-engaging in care. This RFA solicits protocol development and implementation planning, not direct clinical service delivery.

 

The goal of this opportunity is to increase and streamline linkage to HIV care in emergency settings by developing a feasible workflow and protocols for providing ART within seven (7) days of diagnosis, disclosure, or re-engagement. Selected applicants will collaborate with the HCA to design patient-centered procedures that can be integrated into existing clinical operations, reduce delays to treatment, and improve patient outcomes.

 

As of 2024, there were 6,955 PLWH in Orange County who are aware of their HIV status and an estimated 1,706 individuals who remain unaware of their infection. In 2024, 230 individuals in Orange County were newly diagnosed with HIV, and 56 (24%) were concurrently diagnosed with AIDS, indicating prolonged undiagnosed infection prior to testing. Among all PLWH aware of their status, 72.1% achieved viral suppression which is crucial for maintaining health and preventing the transmission of HIV. Additionally, 78.2% received HIV care, and 57.0% were retained in care. For additional local surveillance data, please visit: OChealthinfo.com. OC Health Care Agency | Orange County California - Health Care Agency

summary:
The OC Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking applications from licenses hospital emergency departments to develop practical and sustainable protocols to initiate Rapid Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) for people newly diagnosed with HIV or re-engaging in care.

 

Rapid Antiretroviral Therapy (Rapid ART) Protocol Development is intended to support the development of practical, evidence-based protocols that improve linkage to care for individuals newly diagnosed with HIV and people living with HIV (PLWH) who are re-engaging in care. This RFA solicits protocol development and implementation planning, not direct clinical service delivery.

 

The goal of this opportunity is to increase and streamline linkage to HIV care in emergency settings by developing a feasible workflow and protocols for providing ART within seven (7) days of diagnosis, disclosure, or re-engagement. Selected applicants will collaborate with the HCA to design patient-centered procedures that can be integrated into existing clinical operations, reduce delays to treatment, and improve patient outcomes.

 

As of 2024, there were 6,955 PLWH in Orange County who are aware of their HIV status and an estimated 1,706 individuals who remain unaware of their infection. In 2024, 230 individuals in Orange County were newly diagnosed with HIV, and 56 (24%) were concurrently diagnosed with AIDS, indicating prolonged undiagnosed infection prior to testing. Among all PLWH aware of their status, 72.1% achieved viral suppression which is crucial for maintaining health and preventing the transmission of HIV. Additionally, 78.2% received HIV care, and 57.0% were retained in care. For additional local surveillance data, please visit: OChealthinfo.com. OC Health Care Agency | Orange County California - Health Care Agency

summary:
The Regional Recycling and Edible Food Recovery (RREFR) program provides funding to support projects that advance recycling, waste reduction, and edible food recovery efforts in Orange County. Administered by OC Waste & Recycling (OCWR), the program helps meet state-mandated waste diversion requirements, including Assembly Bill 939 and Senate Bill 1383, which require jurisdictions statewide to recover 20 percent of surplus edible food.

The RREFR grant focuses on expanding edible food recovery countywide. The 2024 Edible Food Recovery Capacity Planning Report projects that, between 2025 and 2034, 40,000 tons of edible food will be landfilled compared to just 10,000 tons recovered. The grant aims to bridge the gap by strengthening regional infrastructure for the safe collection, storage, transportation, and distribution of edible food, and by supporting projects that achieve measurable diversion of edible food from landfills.

 

OCWR hosted a live question and answer virtual session on Thursday, March 19, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. via Zoom. To access the recorded video, please visit OClandfills.com/grants.

Questions may still be submitted through Friday, May 8, 2026.

Due to strong interest and response from the community, OC Waste & Recycling (OCWR) has extended the application deadline for the Regional Recycling and Edible Food Recovery Grant Program to May 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m.

Please review the changes to the timeline and the eligible costs section in the Guidelines and Instructions (PDF).

Subscribe online via OpenGov to receive notifications for Grants page updates.

The County of Orange, Department Name, (hereinafter referred to as County) is requesting competitive bids from qualified vendors (hereinafter referred to as Bidder) to establish a one-time annual contract for Pavement Maintenance and Repair Services under a Job Order Contract (JOC). The JOC provides an on-call, flexible delivery method to address routine, preventative, and/or unplanned airfield and landside pavement needs.  The scope of work includes a range of asphalt and concrete pavement services, such as patching, crack and joint sealing, full- and partial-depth repairs, pavement markings, and related ancillary work. All work shall be performed in accordance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requirements, airport standards, and Part 139 obligations, with strict controls on phasing, night work, safety, and security to minimize impacts to aircraft operations.

summary:
The Regional Recycling and Edible Food Recovery (RREFR) program provides funding to support projects that advance recycling, waste reduction, and edible food recovery efforts in Orange County. Administered by OC Waste & Recycling (OCWR), the program helps meet state-mandated waste diversion requirements, including Assembly Bill 939 and Senate Bill 1383, which require jurisdictions statewide to recover 20 percent of surplus edible food.

The RREFR grant focuses on expanding edible food recovery countywide. The 2024 Edible Food Recovery Capacity Planning Report projects that, between 2025 and 2034, 40,000 tons of edible food will be landfilled compared to just 10,000 tons recovered. The grant aims to bridge the gap by strengthening regional infrastructure for the safe collection, storage, transportation, and distribution of edible food, and by supporting projects that achieve measurable diversion of edible food from landfills.

This RFA is issued to initiate the Q&A period.

2nd RFA will open on March 2, 2026, in OpenGov for application submissions. Upon release, the 1st RFA will close.

OCWR will host a live question and answer virtual session on Thursday, March 19, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Visit oclandfills.com/grants for a virtual meeting link. 

Questions may still be submitted through April 3, 2026 via 2nd RFA.

Subscribe online via OpenGov to receive notifications for Grants page updates.

For technical assistance with OpenGov, please contact OpenGov customer support.

The County of Orange (County) is requesting Statements of Qualifications (SOQ) from interested and qualified firms “Respondent(s)) to provide design and construction services for the Project referenced above (“Project”), to be delivered via Progressive Design-Build (PDB).

 

Respondents shall be firms that satisfy the definition of a Design-Build Entity (DBE) in Public Contract Code (PCC) §22185(c). The DBE shall be either a B-Licensed General Contractor or a lead design firm which will serve as the “Designer-in-Charge,” as defined in California Building Code, or a joint venture firm comprised of both. The DBE shall serve as the prime contracting entity, which shall be clearly identified in the SOQ. If the Respondent can perform only one of the two functions described above, Respondent must identify in its SOQ the firm that will fulfill the other function. For example, if the Respondent is a B-Licensed General Contractor, Respondent must identify the firm it will subcontract with to perform the function of the lead design firm which will serve as the “Designer-in-Charge” in its SOQ. This firm will be referred to as a member of the Design-Build Team (DBT) and shall be afforded protections described in PCC §22185.6(a).

 

Respondents may, but are not required to, include engineers, other design firms, and/or special consultants, in their SOQ submission. These firms will also be referred to as members of the DBT and shall be afforded protections described in PCC §22185.6(a).

summary:
The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency was awarded Community Care Expansion (CCE) Preservation Program funding from the California Department of Social Services to support Adult Residential Facilities (ARF), Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly (RCFE), and Residential Care Facilities for the Chronically Ill (RCFCI). The County is soliciting applications from qualified licensed facilities located within Orange County that are seeking financial assistance in order to provide the CCE Preservation Program funds.

The primary goal of this program is to provide funding for the rehabilitation of eligible licensed adult and senior care facilities that serve Supplemental Security Income/State Supplementary Payment (SSI/SSP) or Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants (CAPI) applicants and recipients, including those who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

Eligible licensed facilities may apply for two forms of CCE Preservation Program financial assistance, with the option to submit a single application for Program I only, Program II only, or to submit for both Program I and Program II (each program requires an individual separate application). 

    1. Program I - Operating Subsidy Payments: Facilities may receive up to $1,000 for each resident who receives either SSI/SSP CAPI. The purpose of this subsidy is to mitigate facility operating deficits and reduce the likelihood of closure. See Section VI (Links to Programs) for specific information. These payments are expected to be issued monthly through March 31, 2029, with the anticipation of funding approximately 25 facilities and benefiting approximately 200 individuals.
    2. Program II - Capital Projects: Funds may be used to cover the cost of physical repairs or required upgrades to prevent facility closure or meet licensing requirements. Projects will be prioritized by health, safety, regulatory compliance, or cosmetic improvements that could help prevent facility closure or a reduction in beds for eligible residents. See Section VI (Links to Programs) for specific information. These payments are expected to conclude by September 30, 2028, with the anticipation of funding approximately 25 facilities and benefiting approximately 200 individuals.

County may award a contract to one or more eligible licensed facilities for each Program and may award one or both Programs to one eligible licensed facility. Further, County award a contract to an eligible licensed facility for both or only one of the Programs in eligible licensed facility’s application.

Eligible licensed facilities must meet the minimum qualifications and requirements as set forth within the RFA, which includes the Implementation Plan and CCE Notice of Funding Availability. Further, County expects the successful eligible licensed facilities to provide the services in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in Attachment B. Model Contract

summary:
As a regional service provider, the County of Orange (County), consisting of 25 departments (and its respective divisions) delivers a broad range of services to the citizens of Orange County. Services provided include public protection, public health, infrastructure maintenance; and community and social services. Orange County Infrastructure Programs provides engineering services for roadways in unincorporated areas and regional flood control programs throughout Orange County. This includes programming, design, legislation tracking, project management, traffic safety, and development support services.

County Counsel is seeking qualified outside counsel to provide real property and related legal services to assist the County and District related to (1) real property matters, including, but not limited to, real estate transactions, leasing (both landlord and tenant issues), licensing, title matters, real estate development, financing, acquisitions, dispositions, public-private partnerships, alternative energy related transactions, federal or state tax code implications, title insurance and survey, environmental matters (including Natural Communities Conservation Plan/Habitat Conservation Plan and state/federal Endangered Species Act), matters concerning California Coastal Commission jurisdiction, construction contracts, California Environmental Quality Act, zoning and entitlement matters ("Real Property Legal Services”); and (2) and real property acquisition and eminent domain related advisory and litigation services (“Eminent Domain Legal Services”).  County Counsel is seeking SOQs from qualified and responsible attorneys or law firms who are willing to enter into the County’s standard Legal Services Agreement and to perform the necessary legal services described herein.  Interested attorneys or law firms may submit information requested in response to this Request for SOQ.

Responsive attorneys or law firms will have the option to submit proposals for (1) Real Property Legal Services; (2) Eminent Domain Legal Services; or (3) both Real Property Legal Services and Eminent Domain Legal Services.  Applying for (1) or (2) or (3) will have no bearing, positive or negative, on the selection process.  Therefore, it is beneficial for respondents to apply for multiple areas of service if qualified.

The County reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to make multiple awards to respondents for services requested in this solicitation.
title: Legal Advisory Services Related to Real Property Legal Services and Eminent Domain Legal Services

Please refer to the General and Funding Information section for anticipated terms of contract(s).

 

Public Facilities & Improvements (PF&I)- Application A

High Priority PF&I projects include:

  1. Parks and Recreation Facilities
  2. Senior Centers
  3. Homeless Facilities
  4. Neighborhood Facilities
  5. Water/Sewer Improvements
  6. Street and Lighting Improvements
  7. Sidewalk Improvements

 

PF&I projects must constitute and meet one or more PF&I High Priority Projects.

Housing Rehabilitation (HR)- Application B

High priority projects for HR are projects that strengthen, preserve, and enhance the physical character and quality of life in Orange County’s low-and moderate-income neighborhoods, including the housing stock.

Applicants may submit Applications for one HR and/or one PF&I project and waitlisted project requested in this RFA. Separate Applications are required for each service type. Complete Application A for Public Facilities and Improvements, and Application B for Housing Rehabilitation.

Metropolitan Cities – Metropolitan Cities will also be funded U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) allocated amounts using the County as Pass Through Entity, and will not have to participate in this RFA process.

summary:
“We want to hear from you!

We invite you to participate in a brief survey that is designed for business owners and business executives in Orange County, California. The office of Orange County Supervisor Vicente Sarmiento is seeking your input to get a clearer picture of the county’s evolving economic landscape. The survey will take approximately 10 minutes to complete. 

The purpose of this survey is to assess how recent federal policy changes may be affecting the county’s business and economic climate. Your feedback is voluntary, will remain anonymous, and will be aggregated with responses from other business leaders across the county and analyzed by researchers at UC Irvine’s School of Social Ecology.

The findings will be shared with the business community this fall to help inform and guide policy and business decisions. Your participation will help provide a clearer understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing businesses in our region.

We appreciate your participation.”

summary:
The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking applications from qualified organizations to provide CalFresh Healthy Living (CFHL) Services to the low-income population residing in Orange County.  The goal of these services is to apply comprehensive, evidence-based obesity prevention strategies that are designed to achieve specific behavioral outcomes, including increased consumption of healthy foods and beverages, reduced consumption of less healthy foods and beverages, and increased levels of physical activity, with the overarching goal of preventing obesity and other diet-related chronic diseases.

 

Poor diets and sedentary lifestyles have a profound impact on the development of obesity and obesity-related chronic diseases. Over the past thirty years, obesity prevalence in the United States has doubled among adults and tripled among children. Obesity and diabetes are major contributors to the leading causes of death, including heart disease, stroke, and certain cancers. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that more than one-third (34.9 percent) of U.S. adults are obese–that is more than 78 million people. In addition, in Orange County, according to the California Health Interview Survey, 60.1 percent of adults are overweight or obese. Obesity is an identified priority area within the Orange County Community Health Improvement Plan. 

 

CFHL is a program of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program-Education (SNAP-Ed) that primarily provides nutrition education to the CalFresh eligible population (generally low-income individuals and families earning less than 185 percent of the federal poverty level). The goal of CFHL is to support the target communities in making healthy food choices and choosing physically active lifestyles. Historically this USDA funding has focused heavily on nutrition education. In 2013, the program shifted to enhance the promotion of physical activity and expand the creation/support of policies, systems, and environmental (PSE) changes that support good nutrition and physical activity.

 

Demonstrating a comprehensive approach to reducing obesity, HCA is seeking to award applications to implement CFHL aligned activities.

summary:
Project Description

The Orange County Flood Control District and the County of Orange has jurisdiction over 380 miles of flood conveyance facilities, and over 35 regional detention basins and dams. The 1986 Orange County Hydrology Manual and 1996 Addendum provides the computational criteria for the estimation of runoff, discharges and volume to size flood control facilities within the county.   

Overview

The purpose of the update to the 1986 Orange County Hydrology Manual and 1996 Addendum is to review the hydrologic procedures, assess the runoff frequencies based on 40+ years of data since the original calibration performed in 1983, and research how climate change and post-fire hydrology can be incorporated into the manual.

Project Description

OCFCD is seeking Proposals from qualified consultants to update the Orange County Hydrology Manual.

summary:
The County of Orange, Health Care Agency (hereinafter referred to as “County”), is soliciting proposals from qualified firms (hereinafter referred to as “Respondents”) for Substance Use Disorder (SUD) Services.  These services are divided into two related programs for special populations: Program 1 - Perinatal and Parenting Residential Treatment and Withdrawal Management Services; and Program 2 – Adolescent Residential Treatment and Withdrawal Management Services.  The primary goal of the two programs is to offer services to those in need of stabilization because of use of alcohol and/or other substances, so the individuals can function in the community utilizing learned coping skills necessary for recovery.  Both Programs shall be housed at 7800 Marine Way in Irvine and shall primarily offer treatment to clients eligible for Drug Medi-Cal benefits. Respondents may apply to provide services in Program 1, Program 2, or both.

Program 1 - Perinatal and Parenting Residential Treatment and Withdrawal Management Services provides treatment within a licensed residential setting to individuals that are pregnant or parenting mothers of children. The primary goal is to stabilize the client in preparation for outpatient treatment.   Services shall include levels of treatment based on the current American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) Level of Care (LOC) Certification or Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) LOC Designation.  

Program 2 – Adolescent Residential Treatment and Withdrawal Management Services provides treatment within a licensed residential setting to individuals aged 12 to 17 years of age.  This program will treat both males and females.  Services shall include individual counseling, psychoeducational groups, clinical groups, withdrawal management and other ancillary services. Referrals and linkage for services are provided at discharge.

County may award a contract to one or more Respondent(s). County expects the successful Respondent(s) to provide the services in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in Attachment A. Model Contract.
title: Substance Use Disorder Services - Perinatal and Parenting Residential Treatment and Withdrawal Management Services and Adolescent Residential Treatment and Withdrawal Management Services

summary:
This Request for Information (RFI) from the County of Orange Information Technology (OCIT) hereby invites qualified Respondents to submit a proposal (including cost) to implement a comprehensive Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platform to enhance the efficiency of County operations, improve citizen engagement, streamline service request management, and foster better communication between government agencies and the community. The platform will serve multiple departments and provide an integrated solution to manage and track service requests, complaints, inquiries, and feedback from citizens. The County currently utilizes the Comcate CRM platform, more on the current platform in the Background section.

The purpose of this RFI is to allow qualified Respondents to present proposals and a presentation to assist OCIT in determining what CRM options are available in the marketplace and to understand current market trends. Upon completion of this RFI, OCIT may issue a formal solicitation or utilize other means to procure a CRM. OCIT may, at its sole discretion, choose not to move forward with a solicitation or procurement.

Please note:

  • Insurance is not required at this time.
  • Only questions sent via the OpenGov online bidding system will be addressed.
  • OCIT desires a cost proposal in the form of:
    • Unlimited seats
    • Annual cost (paid annually)
    • 3 Years


IMPORTANT DATES

RFI RELEASED - April 4, 2025

QUESTION AND ANSWER DEADLINE - April 14, 2025 @ 12PM PCT

PROPOSALS DUE - April 25, 2025 @ 3:00PM PCT

VENDOR DEMONSTRATION - The County may elect to ask proposers for a demonstration. That request, if any, will be made after the RFI closing date and time.

Responses to RFI notices are not offers and cannot be accepted by the County to form a binding Contract,

The County of Orange, Probation, (hereinafter referred to as County) is requesting competitive bids from qualified vendors (hereinafter referred to as Bidder) for the purchase and delivery of Ammunition and Related Supplies. The awarded Contract, (hereinafter referred to as Contract) will be between the County and awarded Bidder, (hereinafter referred to as Contractor) in accordance with the model contract terms, conditions and scope of work. This is a fully electronic solicitation – only electronic bids submitted through the County’s online bidding system will be allowed; no other form of bid submittals will be accepted. Prior to submitting a bid, Bidders are advised to carefully read the instructions below, including the model contract and any solicitation attachments and/or exhibits.

CONTRACTOR REQUIREMENTS

  1. Contractor shall have a place of business within 25-mile radius of County of Orange Probation Department, St. Andrews Campus Training Center, 1700 E. St. Andrew Pl., Santa Ana, CA 92705 to ensure timely pick-up and safety of authorized County personnel.
  2. Contractor shall possess and maintain all Federal, State and local permits, licenses and approvals necessary to provide services/goods required for Ammunition and Related Supplies. Any associated fees shall be the responsibility of the Contractor. Copies of each may be required at time of award or as requested by County.
  3. Contractor shall have a minimum of three (3) years of business experience providing Ammunition and Related Supplies. 

CONTRACTOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Contractor shall:

  1. Provide products specified herein or otherwise agreed to in writing by County.
  2. Place orders as needed. County shall not be subjected to placing minimum orders. 
  3. Package and provide ammunition in bulk, at a minimum of 500 rounds per case, or in a standard 50 round box with 10 boxes per case.
  4. Products supplied shall be new, no irregulars, no seconds, and no substitutions will be accepted. Incorrect delivered/picked-up products shall be replaced with the correct products by the Contractor at the Contractor’s expense within 5 business days from the notification date. All orders must be completed when shipped/picked-up and received by the time specified.
  5. Ensure Winchester manufacturer ammunition listed on Attachment B – Pricing and Compensation is in stock and available for purchase. If Winchester ammunition is not in stock at the time the order is placed, the Contractor has thirty (30) day’s maximum to obtain requested item.
  6. Orange County Probation Department authorized personnel will provide the following when picking up Ammunition and Related Supplies: 1. Ammo Authorization Letter (signed by the head of Agency). 2. Orange County Probation Department Identification Badge. 3. Exemption Certificate
  7. It is the Contractors responsibility to verify the identity of the authorized Orange County Probation Department personnel when picking up an order.

summary:
The Capistrano-Doheny Beach Nature-Based Shoreline Adaptation Project (herein referred to as “PROJECT”) is located alongshore of Capistrano Beach and Doheny State Beach, seaward of the coastal trail at the southeast end of Doheny State Beach and the northwest end of Capistrano Beach, all within the City of Dana Point. Doheny State Beach holds the distinction of being California’s first state beach. Donated by oil tycoon, Edward L. Doheny, for public use in 1931, it was officially renamed as Doheny State Beach in 1963. The beach is one of California’s most popular state beaches, attracting almost one million visitors per year.  The southern end of the state beach features parking near the shoreline.

In 1973, the County of Orange (herein referred to as “COUNTY”) secured a grant through the Land & Water Conservation Fund to acquire 8.5 acres of Capistrano Beach. Then in 1979, Orange County Harbors, Beaches and Parks District, obtained fee simple ownership of the estate. Following this, a General Development Plan was adopted in 1980, paving the way for the construction of a 140-car parking lot, beach entrance, native landscaping, passenger loading area, restrooms, showers, benches, fire rings, two lifeguard towers, and a bicycle storage area.

For many years, these beaches have been subjected to shoreline erosion, resulting in damage to various amenities, and increasing their vulnerability to further erosion, flooding, and inundation. Wave action has undermined the bike path and pavement at Doheny State Beach, leading to the loss of viable parking spaces and exposing some cobble foundations. The southern edge of Doheny State Beach has been particularly affected, with severe erosion compromising the parking lot and turnaround area. Similarly, the north reach of Capistrano Beach has experienced significant erosion, resulting in the loss of amenities including a basketball court and restroom building. While efforts such as the installation of rip-rap and sand-filled geotextile units have provided protection to the backshore, and the sand nourishment projects by OC Parks have temporarily mitigated erosion and enhanced recreational beach areas, the beach continues to face erosion challenges.
title: Capistrano Beach Nature-Based Shoreline Adaptation Project

summary:
The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking applications from qualified organizations to increase capacity to provide Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) and Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) Testing, Care, Navigation and Referral Services to people at-risk for or people living with HIV (PLWH). Qualified organizations will optimize their existing HIV/STI programs and services to increase access to care and improve health care outcomes among populations disproportionately impacted by HIV.

 

This solicitation focuses on the goals and objectives of multiple funding sources including the Health Resource Services Administration (HRSA) Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) Initiative, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) High-Impact HIV Prevention and Surveillance Programs and California Department of Public Health (CDPH), Sexually Transmitted Diseases Control Branch (STDCB) Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) Prevention and Collaboration.  

 

The primary goal of the Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) initiative is to reduce the number of new HIV infections in the United States by 90% by 2030. The EHE initiative focuses on four key strategies or pillars:

  • Pillar One - Diagnose all people with HIV as early as possible;
  • Pillar Two - Treat people with HIV rapidly and effectively to reach sustained viral suppression;
  • Pillar Three - Prevent new HIV transmission by using proven interventions, including pre- exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and syringe services programs (SSPs); and
  • Pillar Four - Respond quickly to potential HIV outbreaks to get needed prevention and treatment services to people who need them.

Goals of the High-Impact HIV Prevention and Surveillance Programs include:

  • HIV and STI testing of Priority Populations who face barriers in accessing testing in medical settings.
  • Increase and Improve linkage of individuals to appropriate prevention, treatment, and care services.
  • Increase and improve linkage to PrEP/Non-occupation Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (nPEP) services.
  • Improve access and utilization of PrEP (HIV per-expose prophylaxis).
  • Improve access and utilization of PrEP Navigation services.
  • Expand Partner Services (notifying individuals who may have been exposed to HIV or and STI).
  • Reducing HIV and STI infection rates in Orange County.
title: HIV/STI Prevention and Treatment Services

summary:
The County of Orange (County) Social Services Agency (SSA) is currently requesting proposals from public, private non-profit organizations, and community collaboratives to provide Families and Communities Together (FaCT) Family Resource Center (FRC) Services.

 

The purpose of this program is to strengthen prevention and intervention services designed to reduce the risk of child abuse and neglect.  Through partnerships, FaCT strengthens our community and is dedicated to promoting stronger families.

 

FaCT is a public-private partnership of the County of Orange SSA.  The partnership is a network of FRCs located throughout Orange County’s highest-risk communities providing essential family support services, education, and resources. 

 

FaCT’s vision is that all our children grow up in stable, nurturing families, and safe supportive communities which promote healthy development and provide opportunities for children, youth, and adults to achieve their full potential as caring, responsible, and productive members of society.

 

FaCT’s mission is to identify and promote promising and best practices, train, fund, and advocate for FRCs to be Orange County’s community-based platform for prevention activities and family support services.

 

SSA is currently requesting proposals to provide services for the following four (4) Service Components:

 

  • FRC Services – Attachment A of the Model Contract
  • Family Stabilization (FS) Services – Attachment B of the Model Contract
  • Elder Adult Support (EAS) Services – Attachment C of the Model Contract
  • Differential Response - Path One (DR – Path One) Services– Attachment D of the Model Contract

 

Proponents must propose for all FaCT services components:  FRC Services, FS Services, EAS Services, and DR-Path One Services.

summary:
The Capistrano-Doheny Beach Nature-Based Shoreline Adaptation Project (herein referred to as “PROJECT”) is located alongshore of Capistrano Beach and Doheny State Beach, seaward of the coastal trail at the southeast end of Doheny State Beach and the northwest end of Capistrano Beach, all within the City of Dana Point. Doheny State Beach holds the distinction of being California’s first state beach. Donated by oil tycoon, Edward L. Doheny, for public use in 1931, it was officially renamed as Doheny State Beach in 1963. The beach is one of California’s most popular state beaches, attracting almost one million visitors per year.  The southern end of the state beach features parking near the shoreline.

In 1973, the County of Orange (herein referred to as “COUNTY”) secured a grant through the Land & Water Conservation Fund to acquire 8.5 acres of Capistrano Beach. Then in 1979, Orange County Harbors, Beaches and Parks District, obtained fee simple ownership of the estate. Following this, a General Development Plan was adopted in 1980, paving the way for the construction of a 140-car parking lot, beach entrance, native landscaping, passenger loading area, restrooms, showers, benches, fire rings, two lifeguard towers, and a bicycle storage area.

For many years, these beaches have been subjected to shoreline erosion, resulting in damage to various amenities, and increasing their vulnerability to further erosion, flooding, and inundation. Wave action has undermined the bike path and pavement at Doheny State Beach, leading to the loss of viable parking spaces and exposing some cobble foundations. The southern edge of Doheny State Beach has been particularly affected, with severe erosion compromising the parking lot and turnaround area. Similarly, the north reach of Capistrano Beach has experienced significant erosion, resulting in the loss of amenities including a basketball court and restroom building. While efforts such as the installation of rip-rap and sand-filled geotextile units have provided protection to the backshore, and the sand nourishment projects by OC Parks have temporarily mitigated erosion and enhanced recreational beach areas, the beach continues to face erosion challenges.
title: Capistrano Beach Nature-Based Shoreline Adaptation Project

summary:
The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking applications from qualified organizations to provide Narcotic Replacement Therapy (NRT) Treatment Services to Orange County residents who have Drug Medi-Cal. The target population for these services is those aged 12 years and older who meet medical necessity criteria for opioid use disorder or another qualifying substance use disorder (SUD) diagnosis. The target population includes both perinatal and non-perinatal individuals. 

Organizations who are contracted through this process would provide NRT (methadone maintenance) and other medication services to clients with a qualifying SUD diagnosis 365 days per year, in an outpatient setting and/or through a mobile NRT unit if the organization’s Narcotic Treatment Program (NTP) license allows it to render services via a mobile unit. Such services include assessment and treatment planning, medication management, individual counseling, group counseling, case management, referral for ancillary needs, coordination of care, discharge planning, Recovery Incentives program, peer services, and linkage to ongoing care, if applicable.
title: Drug Medi-Cal Narcotic Replacement Therapy Treatment Services

Discharge Medication Services. These services are essential for the implementation of California Advancing and Innovating Medi-Cal (CalAIM), aimed at creating a more coordinated, person-centered, and equitable health system that works for all Californians. Through the CalAIM initiative, Medi-Cal members have access to new and improved services to receive well-rounded care that goes beyond the doctor’s office or hospital and addresses all physical and mental health needs. The CalAIM Justice-Involved Initiative allows eligible Californians who are incarcerated to enroll in Medi-Cal and receive a targeted set of services in the 90 days before their release. This initiative aims to ensure continuity of health care coverage and services between the time they are incarcerated and when they are released. It also provides people who are reentering the community with the prescribed medications they need, and access to programs and services to support this important transition.

 

Through this solicitation, County aims to engage qualified, Medi-Cal enrolled pharmacies to fill a full supply of all active medications upon release for incarcerated individuals receiving pre-release services. Full supply is defined as the maximum amount that is medically appropriate and allowed by the Medi-Cal State Plan.

 

County intends to award a Contract for a term up to three (3) years in duration, renewable for two (2) additional one (1)-year periods.

summary:
The County of Orange (County) Social Services Agency (SSA) is currently requesting proposals from public, private non-profit organizations, and community collaboratives to provide Families and Communities Together (FaCT) Family Resource Center (FRC) Services.  

 

The purpose of this program is to strengthen prevention and intervention services designed to reduce the risk of child abuse and neglect.  Through partnerships, FaCT strengthens our community and is dedicated to promoting stronger families.

 

FaCT is a public-private partnership of the County of Orange SSA.  The partnership is a network of FRCs located throughout Orange County’s highest-risk communities providing essential family support services, education, and resources. 

 

FaCT’s vision is that all our children grow up in stable, nurturing families, and safe supportive communities which promote healthy development and provide opportunities for children, youth, and adults to achieve their full potential as caring, responsible, and productive members of society.

 

FaCT’s mission is to identify and promote promising and best practices, train, fund, and advocate for FRCs to be Orange County’s community-based platform for prevention activities and family support services.

 

SSA is currently requesting proposals to provide services for the following four (4) Service Components:

 

  • FRC Services – Attachment A of the Model Contract

 

  • Family Stabilization (FS) Services – Attachment B of the Model Contract

 

  • Elder Adult Support (EAS) Services – Attachment C of the Model Contract

 

  • Differential Response - Path One (DR – Path One) Services– Attachment D of the Model Contract

 

Proponents must propose for all FaCT services components:  FRC Services, FS Services, EAS Services, and DR-Path One Services.

summary:
The State Legislature is considering Assembly Bill (AB) 2557 as early as Monday August 5th. This bill will adversely impact the County’s ability to continue its partnership with your organization.  

 

The Orange County Board of Supervisors opposes AB 2557 because it will place costly, impractical, and burdensome requirements on local agencies that contract with vital service providers, such as non-profits, community-based organizations, and other private entities.  Please see the key provisions listed below. 

 

The Orange County Board of Supervisors opposes Assembly Bill 2557, and lending your voice will make a difference.  

Let Orange County’s legislators know your opposition to AB 2557 in five easy steps:

  1. Click View Opportunity at the bottom of this notice.
  2. Click Draft Response.

  3. Select your entity type and open the attached template letter and fill in the highlighted sections which will become your entity's response letter.

  4. Copy and paste it on your organization’s letterhead, sign it and save as a PDF.

  5. Submit your response using only one of the two methods below before Response Submission Time on Response Submission Date.

    • Electronically through this Portal; or
    • Email it to LegAffairs@ocgov.com

The Leg Affairs team will deliver your letter to the County’s legislators in Sacramento.

 

Key Provisions of AB 2557:

 

Notification Requirements (Effective January 1, 2025)

    • The County must provide reasonable written notice to the employee organization before beginning a procurement process to contract for services currently or previously performed within the last five years by county employees. This notice must include: 

 

    1. The proposed contract and justification. 
    2. Expected contract length. 
    3. Effect on represented classifications.  

 

    • Notification must also be provided at least 30 days in advance of modifying or renewing the contract. 
    • Requirements apply to temporary help contracts exceeding 60 days. 

 

Posting Requirements (Effective July 1, 2025)  

 

    • The County will be required to post on its website any solicitation for, and awarding of, a special services contract greater than $100,000 to perform functions currently or previously performed within the last five years by county employees represented by an employee organization. 
    • Any related documents required by the contract, such as performance reports, will be posted online.

 

Contract Disclosure Requirements (Effective July 1, 2026)

 

    • Each contract posted on the County’s website must include the following:

 

    1. Objectives, deliverables, and goals
    2. A list of all financial expenditures associated with the delivery of services, including personnel costs, direct and indirect expenses, and corresponding deliverables.
    3. The number of each contractor and subcontractor(s)’ employees and independent contractors, organized by job category.
    4. The names of subcontractors providing services.
    5. The hourly rates, total compensation, and pay scales of employees and independent contractors, organized by job classification. (Total compensation includes hourly pay, overtime pay, benefits, and retirement.)

 

    • All required records provided to the County by the contractor will be subject to the California Public Records Act.

 

Organizations like yours are uniquely qualified to meet specific community needs. At a time when local agencies and organizations are doing more with less, new mandates would divert scarce resources and compromise the services of our residents.

 

Thank you for your partnership with the County of Orange.  Please email LegAffairs@ocgov.com if you have any questions.
title: Urgent Action Needed: Oppose Assembly Bill 2557 (Ortega)

summary:
Project Objectives

The Trust intends to outsource the fulfillment and servicing responsibilities of the Program to an experienced firm, aiming to achieve efficient, cost-contained, and legally compliant loan administration. While the firm will handle the administration of the loans, the Trust will retain responsibilities for promoting and disseminating information on the Program. Additionally, the Trust will manage and select potential applicants from the interest list on the Trust website. Furthermore, the Trust will review and provide final approval based on the firm’s underwriting, ensuring compliance of the participating homeowner with the Program terms. All proposals must demonstrate an understanding of and account for the unique design of the Program which is detailed in the supporting Program documents and includes: - Construction-to-permanent loan - Secured on primary residence as a 2nd or 3rd position lien dependent on other financing of the remaining construction costs - 20 years deferred - Partially forgivable, applied halfway through the loan period - Due at Maturity - Interest rate adjustments based on borrower performance - Three distinct interest periods, one period with three possible interest rates that change intermittently - Last-in funding, possibly necessitating a dry-close of the loan - Minimal underwriting standards - No escrow (can ride along another loan that uses an escrow account) Technical Assistance - Validate that the Program and Trust meet all legal and regulatory requirements for any applicable state or federal laws or regulations and provide guidance if any adjustments are needed to be in legal compliance. - Advise the Trust on lender policies, including loss mitigation, bankruptcy, and refinancing. - Alert the Trust and make necessary adjustments to loan fulfillment and servicing due to future regulatory and legal changes that impact the program. Loan Fulfillment - Create and collect loan applications and make determinations on eligibility per terms of the program (not required to brand fulfillment and servicing in Trust’s name). o Construction: the applicant has submitted evidence that: ▪ Collecting a loan condition document verifying the general contractor/ADU professional has provided a statement that the proposed ADU meets the standards of the city, has mobility accessibility, and provides a detailed, line-item budget. ▪ Receive an acknowledgment letter from the borrower that the ADU has not been completed already with a certificate of occupancy. o Borrower: verify the property is owned by the applicant and occupied by the same. o Finances: ▪ Confirm with title information that the Trust loan will be no lower than 3rd lien, ▪ 90% CLTV, ▪ Loan company to verify sufficient source of funds for the completion of the ADU budget, ▪ Total debt for build is less than 120% of construction costs. - Generate and provide all required and applicable disclosures to applicants. The contracted company will be liable for any errors in the disclosures. - Assess the feasibility of the project and contractor experience. - Coordinate with other lenders to minimize closing costs to the borrower. - Validate the financial contingencies prior to loan closing. - Coordinate loan closings including signing of documents and working with the Trust’s preferred title company to record documents. - NOTE: There is no need to monitor the construction process or approve construction draws. The Trust has already created a Loan Agreement, Regulatory Agreement, Promissory Note, and Deed of Trust for use in this Program. - Provide customer service for applicants throughout the loan application and closing process and maintain an electronic file and where required a paper file, for each borrower. Loan Servicing - Provide diligent and customary loan servicing functions, including set-up of new loans, modifications, payoffs, collections, loss mitigation, defaults, foreclosures, and bankruptcy. - Apply interest rate changes throughout the life of the loan per Program guidelines. - Verify income qualification of tenants using HUD-adjusted income standards. - While the Program allows borrowers to defer all their payments, the company will provide a borrower online account that is secure and allows automatic or occasional payment options. - Provide online, secure portfolio access to accounts for the Trust, with an option to customize portfolio and individual loan reports - Annual loan statements to borrowers and applicable tax forms. - Escrow accounts for property taxes and insurance, if necessary (e.g. borrower does not have a loan on their home). - Transfer of payments to the Trust. - Assist in regulatory and financial audits, as necessary. - Portfolio transfer if required. - Spanish and Vietnamese language staffing is preferred, but not required

summary:
RFA-042-1614484-DMA   Adult Residential Drug Medi-Cal Substance Use Disorder Treatment Services - Project 1

The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking applications from qualified Drug Medi-Cal certified organizations to provide Drug Medi-Cal (DMC) Substance Use Disorder (SUD) Residential Treatment Services.  These services will be provided as part of a Drug Medi-Cal Organized Delivery System (DMC-ODS), a continuum of care modeled after the American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) criteria for substance use disorder treatment services.  The primary goal of these services is to provide DMC beneficiaries access to SUD treatment and provide a system of care that helps them achieve sustainable recovery, and to reduce substance use within the community. 

 

The County encourages providers with a specialized focus to apply.  This includes providers that provide services monolingual speakers of beneficiaries that do not speak English.

 

The County has an agreement with DHCS to provide DMC-ODS services through a Prepaid Inpatient Hospital Plan (PIHP).  DMC-ODS shall be available as a Medi-Cal benefit for individuals who meet the medical necessity criteria and reside in Orange County.  The County is seeking DMC certified providers to provide the following residential treatment services, as outlined in the DMC-ODS:

 

  • Level 3.1 Clinically Managed Low-Intensity Residential Services;
  • Level 3.3 Clinically Managed Population Specific High-Intensity Residential Services; and
  • Level 3.5 Clinically Managed High-Intensity Residential Services.

This solicitation is seeking providers of any one or more of the above levels of care for each of the following:

  • Adult DMC SUD Residential Treatment Services; and/or
  • Perinatal DMC SUD Residential Treatment Services;

 

In the Residential Treatment environment, the daily regimen and structured patterns of activities are intended to build positive behavioral patterns within a community. In level 3.3 an individual’s functional cognitive deficits may require treatment that is slower paced, more concrete and repetitive in nature.  Residential services are provided to clients in a program which is maintained and operated to provide 24 hours, 365 days per year SUD Residential Treatment.

 

Components of Residential Treatment services in all three levels include: client-centered treatment  which is based on the client’s and program’s mutual agreed goals/objectives, intake, problem list, individual and group counseling, educational sessions, collateral services, education, relapse prevention; and case management, to address barriers identified at intake which may inhibit clients’ ability to maintain abstinence upon completion of treatment program requirements  such as: housing, employment, financial, social supports, crisis intervention services, discharge planning services, and transportation services. Each treatment program is expected to have an effective collaborative relationship with community, for profit, private and public non-profit providers, community-based organizations, and governmental and non-governmental agencies.  These relationships shall ensure the availability of an appropriate continuum of care to the residents of Orange County. The expectation is that clients will be stable enough to transition to a lower level of care.  The County contracts with various recovery residences/sober living homes in Orange County to provide additional structure and housing for clients who have successfully completed their residential treatment goals. 

 

 

RFA-042-1559048-DMA   Drug Medi-Cal Medically Monitored Withdrawal Management - Project 2 

The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking applications from organizations to provide Medically monitored withdrawal Management Services. These services will be provided as part of a Drug Medi-Cal Organized Delivery System (DMC-ODS), a continuum of care modeled after the American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) Criteria for substance use disorder treatment services. The primary goal of these services is to provide DMC beneficiaries access to SUD treatment and provide a system of care that helps them achieve sustainable recovery, and to reduce substance use within the community.

  

The County has an agreement with DHCS to provide DMC-ODS services through a Prepaid Inpatient Hospital Plan (PIHP). DMC-ODS shall be available as a Medi-Cal benefit for individuals who meet the medical necessity criteria and reside in Orange County. The County is seeking DMC certified providers to provide the withdrawal management services outlined in the DMC-ODS.

 

In the DMC-ODS the ASAM categorizes Medically Monitored Withdrawal Management Services as ASAM Level 3.7. The County is seeking providers for this level of care for adults, ages 18 and over.

 

 

RFA-042-1614003-DMA   Adult residential Drug Medi-Cal Withdrawal Management Services Project 3

 

The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking applications from organizations to provide Drug Medi-Cal Residential Withdrawal Management Services in a non-medical setting, provided the organization has a Drug Medi-Cal Certification.  These services will be provided as part of a Drug Medi-Cal Organized Delivery System (DMC-ODS), a continuum of care modeled after the American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) Criteria for substance use disorder treatment services.  The primary goal of these services is to provide DMC beneficiaries access to SUD treatment and provide a system of care that helps them achieve sustainable recovery, and to reduce substance use within the community.

 

DMC-ODS shall be available as a Medi-Cal benefit for individuals who meet the medical necessity criteria and reside in Orange County.  The County is seeking DMC certified providers to provide the residential withdrawal management services as outlined in the DMC-ODS.

 

Each service program is expected to have an effective collaborative relationship with community, private and public providers, community-based organizations, and governmental and non-governmental agencies.  These relationships shall ensure the availability of an appropriate continuum of care to the residents of Orange County.

 

In the DMC-ODS, the ASAM categorizes Withdrawal Management in five (5) distinct levels of care. As part of this Solicitation the County is only seeking providers of Level 3.2 Clinically Managed Residential Withdrawal Management.

 

Withdrawal Management (WM) services will provide medical and psychosocial interventions to assist the client through acute intoxication and withdrawal to the attainment of a medically stable, fully supported, substance-free state. Additionally, WM services should involve preparing a client for entry into the next level of treatment. Level 3.2 WM, the “social model detox” model, relies more on a supportive, non-hospital environment than on medication to ease the passage through withdrawal.

 

The County encourages providers with a specialized focus to apply.  This includes providers that provide services to monolingual speakers of languages other than English.

The County of Orange (County) is seeking information pursuant to this Request for Information (RFI) from your organization to support in the development of the County’s Request for Proposal for Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) and Partial Hospitalization Program (PHP) Services.  

The responses to this RFI will not constitute an offer for contract with the County and will be solely used by the County to obtain information from providers on service approaches (programmatic operations) providing IOP and PHP program services. The Medi-Cal Billing Manual describes these services as Day Treatment Intensive.  Information is specifically sought for the provision of Day Treatment Intensive services within these IOP and PHP programs. Day Treatment Intensive is a structured, multi-disciplinary program which provides services to a distinct group of individuals. Day treatment intensive is intended to provide an alternative to hospitalization, avoid placement in a more restrictive setting, or assist the beneficiary in living within a community setting. Services are available for at least three hours each day. Day treatment intensive is a program that lasts less than 24 hours 30 each day. Day treatment intensive may include contact with significant support persons or other collaterals if the purpose of their participation is to focus on the treatment of the beneficiary.

Information regarding the Medi-Cal Billing codes can be found at the following link: SMHS Billing Manual May 2024 (ca.gov).

The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking applications from qualified organizations to develop protocols with the purpose of providing Rapid Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) services to people living with HIV (PLWH) in an ambulatory care or emergency setting AND/OR to expand Routine Opt-Out Testing (ROOT) for syphilis, HIV, and Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) through the Emergency Department Screening Program (EDSP) in Orange County. The Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) Grant will fund protocol development for Rapid ART, and the Syphilis Outbreak Strategy Grant by the California Department of Public Health STD Branch will be the funding source for ROOT. The goal of this program is to expand institutions that offer routine opt-out testing and to develop and pilot Rapid ART protocols that detail how your organization will provide patients ART within seven (7) days of HIV diagnosis, or upon a re-engaged patient’s receipt of diagnosis. Organizations will have the option to select one or both activities.

summary:
Consultant Services for Preparation of Five-Year Consolidated Plan and Citizen Participation Plan Update.
 
In accordance with 24 CFR Part 91, the County of Orange is required to prepare and submit to the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) a fiscal year 2025-29 Consolidated Plan (Con Plan).
 
The primary objective of the Request for Proposals (RFP) is to select a Contractor/Consultant to research, outreach (meetings, surveys. etc.), organize and prepare the Con Plan in a manner fully compliant with Federal guidelines 24 CFR part 91 and any changes or revisions therein. The Con Plan will cover Fiscal Years 2025, 2026, 2027, 2028 and 2029 (e.g., FY 2025. The Contractor/Consultant will develop, prepare, and finalize all required components of the Con Plan in accordance with the most current legislation and guidance that consolidates the long-range planning and application aspects of HUD's Community Development Block Grant, Emergency Solutions Grant, and HOME Investment Partnerships Programs into one document. The County's previous Five-Year Consolidated Plan focused on FYs 2020 -25

summary:
The County of Orange (County) Social Services Agency (SSA) is currently requesting proposals to provide Temporary Emergency Group Home (Group Home) Services.  The purpose of this service is to provide alternative emergency placement for dependent and non-minor dependents who require a more individualized program and treatment regime than can be offered in home-based care, STRTPs, or at Orangewood Children and Family Center.

SSA is interested in contracting with nonprofit organizations to provide Group Home services for emergency, short-term shelter to Foster Youth and Non-Minor Dependents (Youth/NMDs) for up to thirty (30) days.   These placements are meant to stabilize Youth/NMDs and assist Youth/NMDs in achieving and demonstrating long-term sustainable behavioral and emotional change with the intent of successfully transitioning to an alternative placement. To accomplish successful transitions Proponents will engage Youth/NMD, parents, any other person(s) deemed appropriate by the assigned Social Worker/Probation Officer, and Youth/NMD assigned Social Worker/Probation Officer.  Eligible Youth/NMDs include dependents who have challenging behavior, mental health and educational needs, and/or probation wards.  The program's goal is to provide temporary care and supervision, assessment, and intensive supportive and stabilization services while determining the best placement option that can meet the Youth/NMD’s needs.
title: Temporary Emergency Group Home Services

summary:
The purpose of Caregiver Support and Engagement service is to increase the local capacity to care for foster children and youth with complex care needs and all need levels in home-based settings, lessen placement disruption and increase the knowledge base and support of caregivers. Recipients of service are caregivers for youth (birth through age 21) who have an open Juvenile Dependency case due to substantiated allegations of abuse, such as physical abuse, sexual abuse, and general neglect. All dependent youth with an opened court case placed in out-of-home care and all foster care providers, including those in the process of becoming licensed, will be eligible for services. 

The goal is to provide on-going and immediate support for caregivers and their families so that caregivers can focus on stabilizing and maintaining youth in their care with the provision of supportive services, unless transitioning to a lower level of care. Caregivers will be coached to grow in caregiver skills, putting these new skills in practice and successfully applying skills to address complex needs of youth. Services will be culturally responsive, individualized, family-centered, strength-based, and needs-driven. Caregivers will be coached to build on the use of naturally occurring community and family supports and resources by increasing the numbers of individuals and entities in their support system. Services will utilize trauma-informed approach, intervention, and engagement strategies. 

Caregiver Support and Engagement Services includes phone support twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days a week, childcare while the caregiver attends/participates in trainings, and reimbursements for mileage and property damage.
title: Caregiver Support and Engagement Services

summary:
County is soliciting proposals from qualified Proposers for Vital Records Management System (VRMS), including the associated professional services for the installation, configuration and implementation of the selected solution. Qualified Proposers should present proposals that will assist County in selecting contractor(s) that will best meet the needs of the Scope of Work described in Section III. Model Contract, Attachment A (Scope of Work) of this RFP.

County will consider a Hosted Solution, which may also be referred to as Software as a Service (SaaS), hosted by either the Proposer or a Cloud Service Provider (CSP), OR a County On-Premise Solution.

The proposed solution must utilize a proven base system/platform, and meet the technical, business, security, and functional requirements as defined in this RFP. The proposed solution must conform to federal, state, local, laws and regulations and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

The solution should enable County to collect, process, share, display, track, report, and otherwise manage electronic records in different formats and associated documents. The proposer is expected to provide implementation services including business workflow definition, integration, configuration of the system, user acceptance testing, training, and post-release support and maintenance. Data conversion and migration from an existing legacy will also be required.

County expects turnkey, configurable solutions with all software, implementation services, training, ongoing maintenance and support provided by the awarded Contractor. Solutions may be submitted by a primary proposer supported by or partnered with subcontractors. Solutions shall not obligate County to manage additional contracts with 3rd party vendors. Therefore, if the solution includes the use of 3rd party software to support the application, County expects the awarded Contractor to deliver its final solution including all supporting software, licensing, and interface development and provide ongoing support and maintenance for such products.
title: Vital Records Management System

The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking proposals from qualified organizations to provide Youth Substance Use Prevention Services in Orange County. The services requested in this solicitation are intended to reduce substance use by youth through the implementation of evidence-based, innovative, and community-defined practices. 

 

Tragic health, social, and economic problems result from the use of alcohol and other drugs by youth. Early initiation of substance use increases the risk for a variety of health and social problems during adolescence, as well as later in life.

 

Alcohol use by people under the age of 21 has significantly declined in the past two decades due to prevention efforts at the federal, state, and local levels. But even with this progress, alcohol continues to be the most widely used substance of abuse among American youth. According to the most recent (2019-2021) California Health Kids Survey data, 11% of Orange County 11th grade students reported past thirty (30) day use of alcohol compared to 14% of California 11th graders. Cannabis/marijuana use during adolescence, a period when the brain is still developing, is associated with negative impacts on brain development, poor school performance, increases in school drop-out rates, and increased risk for psychotic disorders and depression in adulthood. The opioid and illegal fentanyl crisis has had devasting results.  According to the California Department of Public Health, from 2018 – 2021, fentanyl-related overdose deaths among Orange County youth steadily increased.  The 2022 data show a slight decline, however, there is still prevention work to do.

 

Prevention has been defined as “an active process of creating conditions and/or personal attributes that promote the well-being of people” (Lofquist, 1983). Woven within youth prevention services are the principles of youth development, defined as an “ongoing process in which young people are engaged in building the skills, attitudes, knowledge and experiences that prepare them for the present and the future” (Baines and Selta, 1999). The “risk and protective factor” model (Hawkins and Catalano) is supported by research from the National Institute on Drug Abuse. This approach targets interventions to reduce risks and increase protection for young people. Individual protective factors include self-efficacy to say no to substance use and involvement in school and community activities; risk factors can include misperceptions of peer use and low perceived risk of harm.

 

Health disparities exist among groups and are attributed in part to differences in economic status, geographic setting, racial/ethnic identity, as well as social and linguistic isolation.  Thus, prevention services need to be provided to individuals who are underserved, or unserved, particularly from racially and ethnically diverse communities including monolingual non-English speakers, communities of color, recent immigrants, and refugees in Orange County. 

 

The scope of prevention services outlined in this RFP are guided by this definition of prevention and the tenets of youth development.
title: Youth Substance Use Prevention Services

summary:
The primary goal of this program is to support veterans, military-connected individuals, and their family members by:

 

  1. Addressing barriers to accessing behavioral health services (BHS) and other support systems

 

      Veterans, military connected individuals, and their family members struggle in linking to BHS due

      to a variety of barriers including lack of employment, resources, income, and housing. Many are

      unable to link to existing resources through the Veteran’s Administration due to these barriers, while

      others are unable to connect to these resources due to issues such as discharge status or length of

      service times. Providing these support services by peers with actual military experiences or as a

     family member of a veteran, potential participants are more able to avail themselves of BHS Veterans

     Services Program.

 

  1. Addressing the family component of the issues facing Veterans, such as Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Traumatic Brain Injury, substance use, and other mental health issues.

 

By addressing these issues, the goal is to prevent or provide early intervention by training family members to communicate using non-confrontational techniques, with improving knowledge of PTSD symptoms, developing resiliency, and coping skills that will facilitate resolution of family issues. Enhancing the Veterans support system, by strengthening the family unit, will decrease the trauma symptoms that affect the Veterans. Family members will become more resilient and will have improved coping skills which will enable them to recover from their traumas.  Providing services to the family unit will reinforce the important advantage that a family provides in recovering from PTSD and other Behavioral Health issues. 

 

An evaluation of current Behavioral Health Veterans programs suggests family members are often affected by secondary trauma symptoms such as anxiety, depression, and communication issues due to the Veteran’s behavior.  However, some family members lack the understanding and awareness to effectively cope on a day-to-day basis and do not have skills to effectively communicate in a non-confrontational manner.  Additionally, the family member is often intimidated by the physical presentation (perceived intimidation) of the Veterans.  Compounding the issue is the fact that the Department of Veterans Affairs is tasked with serving the Veterans not the Veterans’ families and without another agency with the knowledge, ability, or funding to assist the family members, these families are left with little to no resources. The impact of this gap in services threatens family stability, further contributing to symptoms of trauma. 

 

An offering of peer support services and mental health services to Veterans, military-connected individuals and their families, provides comprehensive support to this vulnerable population
title: Behavioral Health Services and Peer Support for Veterans and Military Families

February 7, 2024

summary:
This Contract is established for the Contractor to provide Advanced Medical Life Support (AMLS) training to various County of Orange Health Care Agency (HCA) Programs.

To elevate clinical nursing practice within HCA, the recommendation is to train registered nurses within various service areas identified by the HCA Project Manager on Advanced Medical Life Support (AMLS).  AMLS remains the gold standard of education for emergency medical assessment and treatment. Endorsed by the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP) and accredited by the Continuing Education Coordinating Board for Emergency Medical Services (CECBEMS), AMLS emphasizes the use of the AMLS Assessment Pathway, a systematic tool for assessing and managing common medical conditions with urgent accuracy.

summary: General work description:  The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking proposals from qualified organizations to provide Crisis Stabilization Unit (CSU) Services. The primary goal of this program is to provide crisis stabilization for clients experiencing acute behavioral health crises that cannot wait until regularly scheduled appointments regardless of the voluntary or involuntary status of the client. CSUs provide outpatient psychiatric stabilization services on a twenty-four seven (24/7) basis, client walk-in as well as police drop-off capability, recovery-focused services (including Peer Mentors) that borrow from the best principles for operating crisis stabilization programs -- while adding components, including provision of medical triage with basic laboratory capability similar to basic urgent care centers. The goal is also to provide better geographic access to services, depending on the provider(s) chosen.

General work description: The County of Orange (County) Health Care Agency (HCA) is seeking proposals from qualified organizations to provide Representative Payee and/or Supplemental Security Income Outreach Services.
The RFP consist of two (2) service programs:
1. Representative Payee Services
2. Supplemental Security Income Outreach Services
Proposers may apply for one (1), or both of the above-listed services. Proposers should submit a fully independent proposal for each service that they are applying for. (e.g. if your organization is applying for both services listed, please submit two [2] complete proposals). Please refer to Section I.G.10 for submittal instructions.
The primary goal of Representative Payee Services is to provide financial assistance and protection from financial abuse and victimization. Many mentally ill individuals experience difficulty in effectively managing their money and other resource allocations. These individuals may lack the ability to organize financial processes and make decisions to pay bills in a timely fashion, as well as lack the ability to exercise the discipline necessary to follow through with a plan. This may result in negative consequences that could impair the client’s recovery, especially in the area of housing, ultimately leading to homelessness and the possibility of more frequent and lengthier hospitalizations.
The primary goal of SSI Outreach Services is to provide assistance in applying for SSI benefits and representation in court to appeal denial of benefits, if required. To achieve stability and the care needed to live a meaningful life, mental health client’s need a program that is dedicated to helping them gain much needed financial assistance to pay for basic needs such as food, clothing, shelter, and access to health benefits that allow for them to receive physical and mental health care.
